stage: Quantitative depth onset, spectral frame budget and gate-error compatibility

completed_results.finite_benchmark: For three frozen tables and all 64-context priors, earliest strict discrepancy >1/20 is five blocks (gap 1/8); earliest >1/3 is seven blocks (gap 7/16).
completed_results.universal_window: For any stationary reversible controller with at most M frame labels and a fixed preparation law, S_D(f-p)>1/20 at D=20(ceil(kappa_M)+1), kappa_M=max_{q<=M} q/abs(sin(q*theta_minus)). This is one common linear contrast over multiple depths, not a common single depth.
completed_results.budget_only_bound: kappa_M<=2*M*4^M; a universal sufficient multi-depth window is at most 20*(2*M*4^M+1).
completed_results.error_compatibility: Uniform block error epsilon_H+epsilon_C >=1/kappa_M is necessary. It is not a sufficient gate-matching criterion.
completed_results.necessary_onset: Point discrepancy >delta requires n>delta/epsilon. The linear contrast >1/20 requires D>1+1/(10*epsilon).

finite_certificates.scope: Earliest times are only for the three named tables. Spectral budgets support a universal multi-depth contrast, not a universal single-depth optimum. No near-sqrt(L) sufficiency claim.

validation.arithmetic: Exact integer, rational and multiquadratic arithmetic. Frozen spectral candidate integers were discovered numerically; final certificates use no floating-point arithmetic.
validation.mathematica_static_check: Balanced brackets, strings and nested comments; no Wolfram kernel execution
validation.latex: 67-page DVI compiled; no overfull boxes or unresolved references; no PDF generated

scope: A completed bounds-and-benchmark stage, not a claim that the full onset optimisation or sqrt(L) onset problem has been solved. Preparation prior is fixed across the multi-depth test.
